chunks: Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Yazid ibn Khalifa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'The time for al-Fajr is from when it begins until it brightens.'

key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: Al-Fajr: the dawn prayer, one of the five obligatory daily prayers in Islam, performed between the first light of dawn and sunrise
key_terms.يَبْدُو: yabdu: to appear, become visible; refers to the first emergence of the true dawn light (al-fajr al-sadiq) on the horizon
key_terms.يُضِيءَ: yudi'a: to become bright/illuminated; indicates the brightening of the sky that precedes sunrise, marking the end of the Fajr prayer window

ai.seo_question: When does the time for Fajr prayer begin and end according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the prayer window for Fajr (dawn prayer) as beginning with the first appearance of dawn light on the horizon and ending when daylight fully brightens. This legal ruling establishes both the start and end boundaries of the Fajr prayer time. The ruling reflects the Islamic jurisprudential principle that prayer times are determined by natural celestial phenomena, and this particular narration was likely given to resolve questions about the precise permissible window for Fajr prayer.
